title: AP-Ready Invoice Packet
user: Solo freelancers who need an invoice accepted by a client's accounts-payable inbox without buying a full accounting suite.

evidence.quote_or_summary: Freelancers describe existing invoice platforms as bloated; one respondent says their practical need is a PDF sent to an AP/finance address.
A self-hosted user requests a download filename containing invoice number, client and date instead of only the invoice number.

recurrence: Two independent invoicing communities expose the same last-mile problem: a technically valid invoice still needs client-readable naming and a clean send packet. Severity is moderate but repeats every billing cycle.
current_workaround: Export a PDF, rename it manually, assemble a payment note in email, and keep a sent-file copy in a folder or spreadsheet.
incumbents_and_gap: FreshBooks, Invoice Ninja and Xero create invoices, but their workflow centers on their own portal/payment flow; a tiny AP attachment pack for email-first clients is not the primary artifact.
smallest_useful_product: Offline PWA that imports a simple invoice CSV/JSON, renders a standards-based PDF, applies an AP-safe filename, and exports a ZIP with PDF, payment instructions and a plain-text email draft. Non-goals: payments, bookkeeping, tax filing or client accounts.
success_measure: In a 30-day pilot, 70% of users send at least three exported packets without manual filename edits.
monetization: one-time — it is a personal recurring utility with no server cost or reason to lock documents in a subscription.
constraints: All data stays local; PDF rendering must support accessible text and locale-aware dates/currency; do not present the output as tax or legal advice.
why_distinct: The product is the email/AP handoff packet, not another invoice ledger or payment processor.

title: PEPPOL Preflight
user: EU microbusinesses and their bookkeepers who need to check a structured invoice before handing it to a paid access point or accounting system.

evidence.quote_or_summary: Business owners discuss mandatory Belgian B2B e-invoicing, expensive/complex intermediaries, and the difficulty of receiving as well as sending structured invoices.
An Invoice Ninja user asks for properly coded electronic-invoice XML export because their country requires it.

recurrence: Regulatory deadlines make this an unavoidable, recurring validation need for small EU sellers; the HN thread includes multiple country-specific paths and access-point concerns.
current_workaround: Trust an accounting vendor, upload a file to a portal, or inspect opaque XML errors after a rejection.
incumbents_and_gap: Access points and bookkeeping suites deliver/send invoices, but a neutral local checker that explains failed fields before submission is rarely the simple first step.
smallest_useful_product: Browser-only validator for a narrowly versioned subset of EN 16931/Peppol BIS inputs, with readable field errors, sample-safe redaction and exportable validation report. Non-goals: becoming an access point, sending invoices, or jurisdiction-specific tax advice.
success_measure: At least 80% of pilot files pass an access-point upload on the first attempt after a Preflight report.
monetization: freemium — free local validation builds trust; paid maintained rule packs can fund regulatory updates.
constraints: Standards/rules must be version-pinned and sourced from official specifications; never claim legal compliance; keep invoice data client-side.
why_distinct: It de-risks the handoff to existing networks rather than competing with access points or accounting systems.

title: Cleared Funds Chaser
user: Freelancers paid by bank transfer/ACH who need to distinguish an invoice being promised, initiated and actually cleared.

evidence.quote_or_summary: A freelancer built a reminder product after manually tracking what clients owed and sending follow-up emails.
A self-hosted consulting business asks not to mark ACH invoices paid until funds arrive, noting transfers can take up to nine days.

recurrence: Two independent accounts identify manual chasing and payment-status ambiguity; it is cash-flow-critical whenever clients pay late or via slow rails.
current_workaround: Mark invoices paid on a promise, leave calendar reminders, or use automated email chasers that do not model settlement state.
incumbents_and_gap: Invoice Ninja, Stripe and reminder SaaS send notices, but their status models often collapse customer action and cleared cash or require payment processing integration.
smallest_useful_product: Local-first invoice-status board with promised/initiated/cleared states, configurable gentle email copy, follow-up calendar export and a one-page cash-at-risk view. Non-goals: bank sync, payment initiation, debt collection or legal late-fee calculation.
success_measure: Pilot users record a cleared date for 90% of tracked invoices and reduce overdue invoices older than 14 days by 25% in two months.
monetization: one-time — payment data should remain under the user's control and the utility works without a hosted service.
constraints: Do not access bank credentials; reminders require explicit user action/export; protect local data with optional encrypted export.
why_distinct: It is a cash-certainty state machine for email-first billing, not an automated collections bot.

title: Reschedule Recovery
user: One-person appointment businesses that lose bookings when a cancellation or reschedule is discussed by phone, text or email.

evidence.quote_or_summary: An Ask HN discussion identifies cancellations and reschedules—not the first reminder—as the hard small-business scheduling problem.
An appointment-booking bug lets mobile users select unavailable dates despite date restrictions working on desktop.

recurrence: The primary request and a separate mobile booking failure both point to high-cost edge cases after a booking is initially made.
current_workaround: Text back and forth, alter a calendar manually, or add a full scheduler/CRM just to send another confirmation.
incumbents_and_gap: Calendly, Square Appointments and vertical CRMs cover broad booking flows; they do not prioritize a small recovery queue for human-originated changes across channels.
smallest_useful_product: A local PWA that stores a booking reference, drafts a two-choice reschedule confirmation, tracks awaiting-confirmation state and exports an ICS update. Non-goals: public booking pages, SMS delivery, payments or CRM.
success_measure: At least 75% of bookings marked changed receive a confirmed new slot or a closed-lost reason within 24 hours.
monetization: one-time — it augments a calendar rather than replacing it and has no mandatory delivery infrastructure.
constraints: ICS output must respect time zones; no customer contact data leaves the device; make confirmation wording configurable for local consumer rules.
why_distinct: It handles the neglected recovery state after a booking, rather than being another public calendar link.

title: Quote Request Capture
user: Small service businesses with a short catalogue and variable work who need to turn a customer request into a complete, answerable quote brief.

evidence.quote_or_summary: A freelancer describes manually moving accepted proposals into invoices and maintaining the same client/pricing details across multiple apps.
A self-hosted user requests client-initiated catalogue quote requests, including visible prices, POA items, stock and prepayment context.

recurrence: Recent requests from both a freelancer workflow and an open-source invoicing community converge on quote intake and the transition from customer request to billing.
current_workaround: Use a contact form, phone notes and spreadsheet, then retype customer and line-item information into a proposal or invoice tool.
incumbents_and_gap: Jobber, HoneyBook and Invoice Ninja can manage broader sales/admin flows; a simple configurable intake that produces a review-ready quote brief is over-served by suites and under-served by forms.
smallest_useful_product: Static embeddable form builder for up to 20 services with conditional questions, photo attachments stored in the browser until export, and a printable/emailable quote-request brief. Non-goals: customer portal, online payment, inventory reservation or automated pricing.
success_measure: At least 60% of submitted briefs contain enough information for the owner to issue a quote without a clarification call.
monetization: one-time — a downloadable embed/template is a better fit than charging a microbusiness for a contact form.
constraints: Published embeds need explicit host-owned privacy copy; attachments must have size limits and direct-download export; no background collection of customer data.
why_distinct: It captures the information needed to quote; it intentionally stops before CRM, proposal e-signature and invoicing.

title: Site Job Proof
user: Tradespeople who need a mobile record of completed work, receipts and customer sign-off before an accountant or invoice system sees it.

evidence.quote_or_summary: A painter seeking testers describes on-site invoicing, accountant reports, bank matching and OCR receipt capture as the everyday mobile-admin problem.
ERPNext users request a canonical receipt field because generic attachments make validation, workflow triggers and e-invoice integrations brittle.

recurrence: A working tradesperson and a mature ERP community independently identify receipts/proof as a critical but poorly structured handoff artifact.
current_workaround: Keep photos in the phone gallery, attach arbitrary files to an invoice, or transcribe them later for an accountant.
incumbents_and_gap: QuickBooks, Xero and field-service suites offer broad job management; their document capture often assumes a cloud account and does not make an auditable job-to-evidence bundle portable.
smallest_useful_product: Offline mobile PWA to create a job card, attach before/after photos and purchase receipts, record customer acknowledgement, and export a dated ZIP/PDF evidence packet. Non-goals: OCR, accounting integrations, dispatch or payment collection.
success_measure: In a four-week pilot, users attach evidence to 80% of completed jobs before leaving the site.
monetization: one-time — the core value is local capture and a portable archive, not a hosted field-service subscription.
constraints: Customer consent for photos/signatures; immutable timestamps should be clearly device-generated, not legally certified; encrypted backups and data-export controls are required.
why_distinct: The deliverable is a portable proof packet, not a general field-service management system.

title: Worklog Appendix
user: Freelancers whose clients dispute billed hours because the invoice has a total but no readable account of completed work.

evidence.quote_or_summary: A freelancer says clients questioned invoice hours because they had no visibility into work until the bill arrived; the issue was transparency, not payment collection.
ERPNext users report timesheets can be pulled into an invoice but corresponding line items still require manual addition.

recurrence: The pattern is repeated in a recent freelancer discussion and in a formal invoice/timesheet feature request: billable detail is disconnected from the invoice a client receives.
current_workaround: Send a raw timesheet CSV, explain hours by email, or manually summarize work in invoice line items.
incumbents_and_gap: Harvest, Toggl and ERPNext track time; their reports are often too detailed for clients or too disconnected from a concise invoice explanation.
smallest_useful_product: Local CSV-to-PDF generator that groups approved worklog rows into client-readable milestones, preserves drill-down rows in an appendix, and produces a matching invoice-line summary. Non-goals: timers, project management, invoicing or employee surveillance.
success_measure: Pilot users see fewer than one hours-clarification request per ten invoices carrying an appendix.
monetization: one-time — it is a private report generator with no account, tracking or team database.
constraints: Data stays in-browser; avoid automatically fabricating work descriptions; support redaction of internal notes and personally identifying detail.
why_distinct: It translates evidence of work into an invoice companion, rather than becoming another time tracker.

title: Quote Section Builder
user: Small businesses selling multi-part jobs who need a quote clients can understand without recreating it outside their accounting system.

evidence.quote_or_summary: A small-business admin-app discussion explicitly groups quotes with invoicing, purchasing, inventory and expenses; an early user uses it to track inventory and send quotes/invoices.
A company says ERPNext lacks grouped/nested quotation headings, forcing it to build a second client-readable quote outside the ERP.

recurrence: Quote creation appears alongside core small-business admin in 2025, while the ERP issue documents a concrete duplicate-document workaround.
current_workaround: Maintain a plain accounting quote plus a second Word/PDF document with rooms, phases or scope headings.
incumbents_and_gap: ERPNext, Xero and QuickBooks handle line items; rich proposal products add signatures and CRM. A focused sectioned quote renderer sits between those extremes.
smallest_useful_product: A browser-only editor that imports CSV line items, groups and nests them into client-facing sections, calculates subtotals, and exports an accessible PDF plus flat CSV for accounting re-entry. Non-goals: e-sign, customer portal, payment, inventory or CRM.
success_measure: At least 70% of pilot quotes are exported without a second document editor being opened.
monetization: one-time — its narrow formatting utility is naturally owned as a local tool.
constraints: Currency/tax totals must be deterministic and visible; do not claim tax correctness; ensure PDF preserves selectable text and PDF/UA-friendly semantics where feasible.
why_distinct: It fixes the client-readable layer that accounting quote forms omit, without growing into a proposal suite.

title: Client Handoff Kit
user: Freelancers and tiny agencies completing a project who need to leave the client with a usable, organized delivery rather than scattered links and credentials.

evidence.quote_or_summary: A five-year freelancer says clients and staff struggled across separate communication, document, knowledge-base and project platforms, motivating an internal client portal.
Invoice Ninja proposes a broader client-facing resource layer for generated files, external links, documents and resources made available after payment.

recurrence: Separate recent accounts show the same delivery sprawl: project documents and knowledge need a client-facing structure even when a full portal is excessive.
current_workaround: Send a long email with Drive/Notion/GitHub links, attach a ZIP, and answer follow-up questions after handover.
incumbents_and_gap: Notion, Drive, Dropbox and full client portals manage content but require accounts, permissions and ongoing hosting; a self-contained handoff artifact is missing.
smallest_useful_product: Desktop/local web generator that turns a folder plus a manifest into a branded static handoff site with checklist, search, links, expiry note and downloadable archive. Non-goals: credential storage, client messaging, collaboration or hosted portal accounts.
success_measure: At least 70% of pilot handoffs receive no follow-up request for the location of a promised file/link within 14 days.
monetization: one-time — an offline build/export tool avoids charging users to retain their own completed work.
constraints: Never include secret values in manifests; warn on likely keys/password files; use an allowlist for executable/HTML content to reduce unsafe handoff bundles.
why_distinct: It produces a portable end-of-project handoff instead of locking a client into another ongoing portal.

title: Early Payment Terms
user: DACH/EU microbusinesses offering early-payment discounts who need a clear, auditable terms calculation without manual credits.

evidence.quote_or_summary: An Ask HN poster asks freelancers which invoicing features matter and what existing tools get wrong or overcomplicate.
A Swiss Invoice Ninja user says cash-discount terms require manual reduced-payment, credit-note and apply-credit workarounds with poor reporting/audit trails.

recurrence: A current request for simpler freelancer billing meets a detailed 2026 report of a regionally common but poorly served payment term.
current_workaround: Calculate the reduction by hand, record a partial payment, issue a credit note, and explain terms in a custom invoice note.
incumbents_and_gap: General invoicing tools offer discounts, but many do not model conditional early-payment terms and their accounting trail cleanly for small users.
smallest_useful_product: Local calculator and PDF-note generator for versioned early-payment terms: amount, cut-off date, discounted balance, and an accounting handoff memo. Non-goals: issuing invoices, recording payments, posting ledger entries or legal/tax advice.
success_measure: In pilots, 95% of generated term sheets match the user's independently checked arithmetic and deadline.
monetization: one-time — a transparent local calculator is preferable to a recurring billing platform add-on.
constraints: Jurisdiction presets must be clearly labeled and maintained; calculation inputs/rounding must be visible; do not represent output as legal or tax compliance certification.
why_distinct: It is a transparent conditional-terms companion, not an invoice system or a late-payment enforcement tool.

title: Pocket Cashflow Calendar
user: Freelancers with irregular income who need a simple, private view of whether scheduled bills fit between expected client payments.

evidence.quote_or_summary: A money-tracker discussion highlights that effective tracking requires thorough, timely logging and that people otherwise fall back to Excel or Notion.
A local-first budgeting user reports incorrectly calculated monthly funding for two annual scheduled bills with different end dates.

recurrence: Both sources expose the fragile edge of cash planning: manual logging is hard, and even established local budgeting schedules can misstate future obligations.
current_workaround: Use a general budget app, spreadsheet or mental buffer; manually move invoice expected dates and recurring bills.
incumbents_and_gap: YNAB and Actual Budget are broad budgeting systems; they do not center a freelancer's small set of expected invoices, tax reserve and dated bills in a one-screen scenario view.
smallest_useful_product: Offline cash calendar with manual expected-payment confidence, dated bills, tax-reserve percentage, and a daily lowest-balance forecast with a CSV import/export. Non-goals: bank sync, double-entry accounting, investment advice or automatic categorization.
success_measure: At least 60% of pilot users update expected payment dates weekly and identify a negative-balance day at least seven days in advance.
monetization: one-time — cash data is sensitive and the utility's value does not depend on aggregation or banking integrations.
constraints: No bank credentials or financial advice; calculations must be reproducible and exportable; local encryption and a plain backup file are essential.
why_distinct: It forecasts the gap between receivables and obligations instead of attempting to replace a complete personal-finance ledger.

title: Offline Stocktake Labels
user: Tiny retailers, makers and storerooms that need a trustworthy physical count and printable labels without adopting a full warehouse ERP.

evidence.quote_or_summary: A local-first barcode tool was built after small businesses faced costly enterprise label subscriptions or had to upload sensitive inventory CSVs to free generators.
An ERPNext warehouse operator requests one scannable identity per variable physical pallet/package so its quantity and movements remain trackable.

recurrence: Recent small-business label pain and a detailed warehouse tracking request show persistent need to connect physical units to counts without exposing inventory data.
current_workaround: Use Excel, paid label software, generic online barcode sites or a much larger inventory package than the workflow warrants.
incumbents_and_gap: BarTender, Shopify inventory and ERPNext serve labeling/inventory broadly; a local count-session tool with lightweight label IDs is too narrow for their main workflow.
smallest_useful_product: Offline PWA that imports a CSV, assigns printable QR/Code-128 labels, records a count session by scan/manual entry, and exports stock deltas plus a count audit sheet. Non-goals: POS, suppliers, multi-location replenishment, shipment tracking or cloud sync.
success_measure: Pilot users finish a 100-SKU count with a reconciled CSV and fewer than 2% unresolved labels.
monetization: one-time — local CSV processing and print/export avoid recurring infrastructure costs and protect commercial inventory data.
constraints: Barcode symbology/print size needs validation; no server upload; design for camera permissions and manual fallback; preserve immutable count-session exports.
why_distinct: It is a count-session and label-audit utility, not a retail POS or warehouse-management clone.
